name: Sunday Harbour View Sukhumvit 50 Hotel
detail: Very good. Even though it's no longer part of the Ibis chain, the quality is still there. The room is small, the air conditioning is cool, the bed is good, and the soundproofing is not great but it’s not bad. It's great to find cheap accommodation in the city. The hotel’s location may not be on the main street, and the entrance looks a bit dark, but the hotel has parking. The staff is lovely, the hot water flows strong, and I slept comfortably. It's very worth the price for what you get.

name: Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel Bangkok
detail: I'm glad I chose this hotel for my first time in Thailand. The room was lovely and clean, and the view of Terminal 21 and the intersection from the window was beautiful. There were always staff members who could speak Japanese, which gave me peace of mind. I apologize for any inconvenience caused with the laundry, but I appreciate their very kind assistance. I would love to stay here again. Thank you very much! ♪

name: Palette Hi Hotel Bangkok
detail: Room with a good location Review of a room that is beautiful, clean, and offers great value. There are various types and sizes of rooms to choose from, ranging from standard rooms to executive suites, which are very spacious, perfect for relaxing whether you're here for work, a getaway with a partner, family, or hanging out with friends. It's very convenient for traveling, close to shopping malls, the sky train, fresh markets, and night markets. Importantly, the staff here are friendly, polite, and provide excellent service. Highly recommended! Hi Hotel Bangkok ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐🥰🥰

name: Furama Silom Hotel Bangkok
detail: To ride BTS, you first need to get to MahaNakhon. However, it's not a big problem in Bangkok because it's easy to use taxis or motorcycles. Also, MahaNakhon is not very far, so you can walk there, and you can see MahaNakhon from the rooftop pool of the hotel. I saw a review mentioning cockroaches, but there were none. However, the lobby and hotel corridors felt a bit scary as the hotel is old. Haha. But the rooms were cleaner than I expected, and the rooms were spacious, which was nice. The air conditioning was great, and the bathroom was large with a decent-sized bathtub, which was good for relieving fatigue. The staff was friendly. I reserved breakfast, but I overslept every day, so I couldn't eat. Haha. The pool isn't very big, but the view is nice, and there’s also a bar with a great view. However, there was not much shade at the pool, so we couldn't stay long. Hahaha. Across the hotel, a pretty nice landmark building is going to be built in Bangkok within a few years. They are working hard on it now. So, I think this hotel will have quite a good location then. Right next to the hotel, there is a 7-11, which was very convenient! The hotel was old and a bit worn out, but the rooms were still comfortable for the price. It’s located in an area where you can enjoy the nightlife, but it's also far enough from that area, so the surroundings of the hotel were quiet, which was nice. In fact, there are many graves in this area. Haha. I always found it cheap on Agoda and debated whether to book it, but it turned out better than expected, making me want to visit again. It seems like one of the few remaining hotels in Silom that offers good value for the price.

name: Maison Hotel Bangkok
detail: The location was perfect and the staff were exceptionally helpful, making the stay very comfortable. The facilities, including parking and breakfast, were top-notch, and the cleanliness throughout was impressive. The bathroom was well-maintained, and the sleep quality was excellent, complemented by a nice view. Overall, great value for money with no negatives to report.

name: The Landmark Bangkok
detail: This was a last-minute booking due to a flight delay, but it turned out to be the kindest and most comfortable place among the three accommodations I stayed at during this trip. Although it's an older establishment and not a trendy new hotel or an Instagram-worthy spot, the details of older Bangkok hotels that can’t be seen in newer ones are great, and the service from the staff is very comforting. In fact, it’s not uncommon to encounter expensive places where faucets splash a lot, toilets are too high, or amenities that feel overpriced and barely useful. However, here everything felt just right, not too little and not too much, tailored perfectly for guests. They allowed early check-in two hours before our scheduled time and offered late check-out at 4 PM. Additionally, you can enjoy cocktails and a variety of finger foods for free while watching the night view from the 31st-floor lounge. The swimming pool is 2.6 meters deep... Later, I borrowed some tape for my luggage, and they were more than happy to lend it. Thanks to Clovis at the reception, I was well-fed with a really delicious latte, complete with rich milk foam, and I arrived at the airport with ample time to spare. It's located right in front of Nana Station, making it easy to go anywhere, and I was truly disappointed to have only spent one night there. The breakfast might not have a wide variety, but it is prepared with care rather than just relying on seasonings, and the coffee is absolutely the best. Sipping coffee while gazing at the skyscrapers in the morning made me not want to go home. I recommend this place to those who miss classic hotel service. The lounge view of the city is stunning, so skip the rooftop bar and come here instead!

name: Dang Derm Khaosan
detail: I chose this hotel for my stay on Khao San Road, and overall it was a very good hotel. The hotel was clean with a calm atmosphere, contrasting with the liveliness of Khao San Road outside; the lobby and corridors were quiet and comfortable. The room was spacious, well-cleaned, and the bed was very comfortable. The air conditioning worked well, and the shower's water pressure and temperature were stable, making my stay very pleasant. The amenities were also adequately provided, and I felt it was a cost-effective hotel overall. What I particularly liked was the pool, which was well-maintained and allowed for relaxing breaks between sightseeing. It was a rare space to rest quietly away from the hustle and bustle of Khao San Road. The staff was courteous and friendly right from check-in. They provided pleasant explanations for directions and local information, making my stay reassuring. However, one disappointing aspect was that it seemed like someone had rummaged through the bags I left in the room. While nothing was stolen, the arrangement of items in my bag was clearly different, which made me uneasy. When I consulted the front desk, they responded politely, but I hope this issue can be improved. Therefore, I believe it's important for future guests to take care of their valuables. I recommend using the safe and being cautious during your stay. The location is perfect, just a short walk to the center of Khao San Road. There are plenty of street vendors, restaurants, convenience stores, and massage options, so I had no trouble with meals or shopping. Overall, it was a very good hotel, but the luggage issue was disappointing. Aside from that, it was a comfortable and appealing hotel, and if the issue is addressed, I would like to return.

name: ibis Styles Bangkok Sukhumvit Phra Khanong
detail: The cleaning is thorough and very clean! The pool isn't large, but the atmosphere is nice, and we enjoyed it even with kids! The staff were also very accommodating, there was a kids' club, and they provided a baby crib, making it perfect for a family vacation! It's a bit of a walk from the station, but it wasn't a problem when we used Grab to get around! There's also a local market nearby, and it was truly a wonderful stay!

name: Asia Hotel Bangkok
detail: It was great to be directly connected to the station since it was the rainy season. I could leave my luggage anywhere and go out again. There was no balcony, but the room was spacious, clean, and comfortable. There was a bathtub, which allowed me to enjoy a luxurious time. There wasn't an electric kettle, but there was a hot water server in front of the elevator. I wanted to drink coffee as soon as I woke up, so I brought paper cups and instant coffee with me. The hotel staff was also friendly. I had previously stayed at cheap hotels nearby that cost about 1,000 baht per night, but this time the hotel was about 1,700 baht per night. This quality is worth the price. I plan to stay at this hotel again the next time I go to Bangkok.

name: Boss Suites Nana
detail: It was about a 10-minute walk from the train station, so the access was good. The receptionist spoke a little Japanese. I was having trouble figuring out how to get the shower water to come out, but when I told the front desk, they came to my room with me and assisted me.
